rows: Aberglaslyn Pass, Wales

This photochrom, made by the Detroit Publishing Company in the 1890s, shows a rocky pass in Snowdonia, Wales, where a river runs between steep wooded slopes. Photochroms were color prints made from black-and-white photographs using inked stones.
How do you think color was added to a black-and-white photo?
Pont-y-Pair, Betws-y-Coed
Pont-y-Pair is an old stone bridge over the River Llugwy in north Wales, and tourists loved to visit it. This photochrom shows the water rushing among the rocks under the arches.
How many arches do you see?
Cadair Idris and the Dysynni Valley
This photochrom shows Cadair Idris, a mountain in Wales, rising above a valley with cattle grazing. Welsh legend says anyone who sleeps on the mountain wakes up a poet or a madman.
Would you try sleeping on Cadair Idris?
Snowdon from the Carnarvon Road
This photochrom, made about 1890, shows Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales, rising behind a road. Printed in many colors, it was sold to tourists.
How high do you think the mountain is?
From the Tweed, Abbotsford
This is Abbotsford, the house of the author Sir Walter Scott, as seen from the River Tweed in Scotland. Scott's novels made Scotland a favorite place for tourists.
Why would readers visit a writer's house?
The Black Watch Monument, Aberfeldy
The Black Watch Monument near Aberfeldy in Scotland honors a Highland regiment. A soldier in a kilt stands on top, and this photochrom shows it in the countryside.
Why do monuments often have a soldier standing on top?
Ailsa Craig, Scotland
Ailsa Craig is a rocky island that rises out of the sea off the coast of Scotland. It is famous for its granite, which is used to make curling stones.
What do you think the island is like up close?
Irish Colleen
A young Irish girl, called a colleen, poses for a photochrom made by the Detroit Publishing Company. Pictures of country people were popular with tourists in the 1890s.
What is she wearing?
Irish Jaunting Car
A jaunting car is a light two-wheeled carriage where passengers sit back to back, used in Ireland. This photochrom shows tourists' favorite way of getting around.
Would you like to ride in a jaunting car?
Cliffs of Moher, County Clare
The Cliffs of Moher in Ireland rise about 200 meters above the Atlantic Ocean. This photochrom from the 1890s shows the towering cliffs.
How tall are 200 meters compared with a building?
Eccles Hotel, Glengarriff
A photochrom of the Eccles Hotel in Glengarriff, County Cork, Ireland. The hotel was popular with tourists who came for the mild climate and the harbor.
Why do people stay in hotels when they travel?
Maplewood Farm, Woodstock Valley, Connecticut
This photograph shows a farm in a valley in Connecticut around 1890. Barns and trees spread across the hills of rural New England.
What do you think a farm morning is like?
Excavation at Pompeii, Italy
Benjamin West Kilburn made a stereograph of the excavations at Pompeii, the Roman town buried by the volcano Vesuvius in the year 79. Digging uncovered streets and houses just as people left them.
What would you find if you dug up a whole town?
Zacatecas from Below the Railroad Station
The Detroit Publishing Company photographed the old mining city of Zacatecas, Mexico, in the 1890s. The city of silver mines lies in a bowl of hills.
Why do mining towns grow in hills?
Guanajuato, Mexico
This panorama shows Guanajuato, a colorful city in Mexico built in a narrow valley, in the 1890s. Houses of every color climb the hillsides.
How would you get around in a city built on hills?
Weeping Magdalen
Charles I. Berg made this photograph, number 5 in the portfolio American Pictorial Photography, in 1892. Pictorialists aimed to make photographs look like paintings, with soft focus and moody poses.
Why would a photographer want a photo to look like a painting?
Wet Night, Columbus Circle, New York
William A. Fraser photographed a rainy night at Columbus Circle in New York in 1892. Wet streets and glowing lights give a mood that painters loved.
What do rain and lights do to a street at night?
Tomb of Walt Whitman
This photograph shows the granite tomb of the poet Walt Whitman in Camden, New Jersey, around 1892. He designed the stone house-like tomb himself before he died.
Why would someone plan their own tomb?
Bear Lake, Lehigh Valley Railroad
William H. Rau photographed Bear Lake in Pennsylvania in 1893. Railroads hired photographers to take scenic pictures to attract tourists.
Why would a railroad want pretty pictures?
Mending Nets, Katwijk
A photographer made this picture of women mending nets in Katwijk, a fishing town in the Netherlands, in 1894. Nets needed constant repair, and women often did the job.
How would you mend a big net?
Harvesting, Black Forest
Alfred Stieglitz photographed workers harvesting in the Black Forest in Germany in 1894. He wanted to show the beauty of ordinary work.
What are the people doing in the field?
Winter Landscape
Clarence H. White photographed a quiet winter landscape in about 1895. White was a leading pictorialist who later taught many great photographers.
What sound does a winter field make?
Landscape by William B. Post
William B. Post photographed landscapes in Vermont around the turn of the 20th century. He often photographed in snow.
Why would a photographer like winter?
Confederate Monument, Oakwood Cemetery, Chicago
This monument at Oakwood Cemetery in Chicago was dedicated in 1895 to Confederate soldiers who died in a prison camp. It towers over the graves.
Why would a cemetery have a big monument?
Meeting of Day and Night, Lake George
Alfred Stieglitz photographed a scene at Lake George, New York, in 1896. The title describes the hour between sunset and darkness, when light fades.
What colors does the sky turn between day and night?
Along the Old Canal
Clarence H. White photographed a quiet canal in Ohio in 1896. A woman and a path run alongside the water in soft light.
What does a canal path feel like?
What Shall I Say?
Clarence H. White photographed this posed picture of a woman writing, with the title What Shall I Say? in 1896. White made quiet scenes of family life in Newark, Ohio.
What do you think she is writing?
Lunar Photograph: Copernicus, Kepler, Aristarchus
Maurice Loewy and Pierre Puiseux photographed the Moon through a telescope at the Paris Observatory in the 1890s. Their huge atlas of the Moon helped astronomers map its craters.
How do astronomers map the Moon?
Arnold Genthe with a Woman Friend
Arnold Genthe photographed himself seated outdoors with a woman friend in the 1890s. Genthe was a German-born photographer who settled in San Francisco.
Why would a photographer be photographed?
Princess Angeline

Edward S. Curtis photographed Kikisoblu, called Princess Angeline, in Seattle in 1896. She was the daughter of Chief Sealth, for whom Seattle is named, and she lived in a small house on the waterfront. This portrait was one of Curtis's first big successes.
Why would a famous photographer pick her as a subject?
A Chinese Boy, Chinatown, San Francisco
Arnold Genthe photographed a boy in San Francisco's Chinatown in the 1890s. Genthe made hundreds of secret pictures of the neighborhood with a hidden camera.
What do you think the boy is looking at?
Genthe Photographing Writers
Genthe photographed a group of friends including the poet George Sterling, the writer Mary Austin and Jack London. Writers loved to visit his studio in Carmel.
Why would writers be friends with a photographer?
Young Woman Holding Roses
James Arthur made this picture as art, which was a radical idea in the 1890s. A young woman holds roses in soft light, like a painting.
Why was it radical to call a photograph art?
Clarence H. White Sr.
Gertrude Käsebier photographed Clarence H. White Sr., a fellow photographer, in 1897. They were friends in the Photo-Secession and pushed for photography as art.
What do you think the friends talked about?
After the Massacre, Christian Quarter, Canea
Underwood and Underwood photographed a ruined street in Canea, Crete, in 1897 after a conflict. The picture was sold as a stereograph to people at home.
Why would people at home want to see this?
Denver, Colorado, with Snowy Range
The Detroit Publishing Company photographed Denver in 1897 with the snowy Rocky Mountains in the distance. The mountains stand tall behind a growing city.
How does a city look with mountains behind it?
Telegraph Poles
Clarence H. White photographed a row of telegraph poles in 1898. The poles stand like a rhythm of lines against the sky.
Why are telegraph poles interesting to look at?
An Icy Night
Alfred Stieglitz photographed New York City on an icy night in 1898. The glow of lamps and the icy sheen show how he loved bad weather.
What would you wear on a night like this?
Columbus Avenue Station, Boston
Charles S. Harrington photographed the Columbus Avenue station of the Boston and Albany Railroad in 1898. The East end of the line had tracks lined with signals and cars.
What does a station feel like when a train arrives?
Grant's Tomb, Riverside, New York
Keystone View Company made a stereograph of Grant's Tomb in New York in the 1890s. The huge granite tomb honors General Ulysses S. Grant, the Civil War hero and 18th president.
Why would a general have such a huge tomb?
Columbia Glacier from Heather Island, Alaska
Edward S. Curtis photographed the Columbia Glacier in Alaska in 1899 as part of the Harriman Alaska Expedition. He was the official photographer on the trip.
How would you get to Alaska in 1899?
Sixth Avenue, New York
Underwood and Underwood photographed Sixth Avenue in New York in 1899, when horse carts and elevated trains shared the street. The elevated railway ran above the avenue.
What sounds would you hear?
Schoolgirls Doing Calisthenics
Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed schoolgirls doing exercises at the Hampton Institute in Virginia around 1899. She documented the school for the Paris Exposition.
What exercises would you do?
Old-Time Cabin
Frances Benjamin Johnston photographed two African American men and a cabin at the Hampton Institute in Virginia in 1899. She was one of the first women press photographers.
What does the cabin tell you about the people?
Spring (A Triptych)
Clarence H. White made a triptych, a picture in three parts, called Spring in 1899. Women in white dresses stand in an orchard of blooming trees.
How does a triptych tell a story?
The Cliff House, San Francisco
The Detroit Photographic Company photographed the Cliff House, a famous restaurant on a cliff above the Pacific in San Francisco, in 1899. Tourists loved to see the sea lions on the rocks below.
Would you like to eat on a cliff above the sea?
Tree in Snow, New York City
Alfred Stieglitz photographed a tree in the snow in New York City around 1900. The tree stands like a drawing against the white.
How does snow change the look of a tree?
Eggs of a Stone-Curlew or Plover
Richard Tepe photographed the eggs of a stone-curlew, a bird that nests on the ground. The speckled eggs are hard to see on the pebbles.
Why are the eggs speckled?
Krishna's Butter Ball, Mahabalipuram

An unknown photographer photographed Krishna's Butter Ball, a huge boulder balanced on a slope at Mahabalipuram in southern India. It looks as if it could roll, but it has stood still for over a thousand years.
Why doesn't the giant rock roll away?
Crossing the Missouri River by Bridge
Agnes Winterbottom Cooney photographed the crossing of the Missouri River in Nebraska around 1900. She was an amateur who documented family life on the Plains.
How would you cross a big river?
Chief Flying Hawk
Gertrude Käsebier photographed Chief Flying Hawk of the Oglala Lakota in 1898. He was in Buffalo Bill's Wild West show, and Käsebier made dignified portraits of the performers.
How does the portrait show respect?
Chief Iron Tail
Gertrude Käsebier photographed Chief Iron Tail, a Lakota man who traveled with Buffalo Bill's Wild West show, in 1898. His portrait was one of her best known.
What do you notice about his face?
Bengal Lancers Escorting Alfred
Underwood and Underwood photographed Bengal Lancers on parade as part of an event for a British prince. Their turbans and lances made them look grand.
What do the lancers' uniforms look like?
Olive Edis
This is an autochrome, an early color photograph on glass, of the British photographer Olive Edis. Autochromes, which first appeared in 1907, used dyed starch grains to make color.
How do you think starch grains make color?
Truman Newberry and His Wife
Bain News Service photographed Truman Newberry, a Detroit businessman and later senator, and his wife. George Grantham Bain's news photo agency covered many famous people.
Why would a news agency photograph politicians?
Selma Lagerlöf
Selma Lagerlöf was a Swedish writer who wrote The Wonderful Adventures of Nils. She became the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1909.
Have you read any stories by Selma Lagerlöf?
The Western Promenade, Portland, Maine
The Detroit Publishing Company photographed the Western Promenade, a hilltop park, in Portland, Maine, around 1900. Ladies in long dresses stroll along it.
What would you do on a hilltop walk?
Schenley Park, Pittsburgh
The Detroit Publishing Company photographed Schenley Park in Pittsburgh around 1900. The park was a gift to the city and gave people green space in the smoky industrial town.
Why would a smoky city want a park?
President Carter, Summer in the Parks
Warren K. Leffler photographed Jimmy Carter for the Summer in the Parks program at the White House in the 1970s. The LoC date for this image is wrong.
Why would a president visit a park?
Versailles, Corner of the Park
Eugène Atget photographed the park of Versailles in 1901 at dawn, when no one was around. He made hundreds of pictures of the empty gardens.
Why would you photograph a garden at dawn?
Versailles, the Rhône by Tuby
Atget photographed a statue of the Rhône river god by Jean-Baptiste Tuby at Versailles in 1901. The reclining river god sits among the fountains.
What does a river god look like?
Versailles, the North Basin
Atget photographed a basin of water in the north gardens of Versailles in 1901. His pictures of fountains and statues were bought by artists.
Why would artists buy photographs of gardens?
When the Sands Are Running Low
Gertrude Käsebier made this portrait in 1901. A woman and a girl look at an hourglass, and the picture is about passing time.
What does the hourglass mean?
F. H. Evans
Gertrude Käsebier photographed Frederick H. Evans, the English photographer of cathedrals, in 1901. Käsebier met many photographers in London.
Why would one photographer photograph another?
Boylston Station Platform, Boston
The Boston Elevated Railway photographed the south end of a platform at Boylston Station in June 1901. The subway, started in 1897, was the first in America.
What was it like to ride the first subway?
Kitty Stieglitz, Central Park
Alfred Stieglitz photographed his daughter Kitty in Central Park, New York, in 1901. Fathers were often the best photographers of their families.
Why would a father take lots of pictures of his daughter?
Indian Chief
Gertrude Käsebier photographed a Native American man in Wild West show costume in 1901. Her pictures were dignified portraits of people who were often treated as curiosities.
How do you want to look in a portrait?
Alfonso XIII of Spain
Alfonso XIII was king of Spain from the day he was born in 1886 until 1931. This portrait by Underwood and Underwood was made when he was still a teenager.
What would it be like to be a king from birth?
Lead, South Dakota
The Detroit Photographic Company photographed Lead, a gold mining town in the Black Hills of South Dakota, around 1901. The Homestake Mine, the biggest gold mine in America, was there.
What would life in a mining town be like?
The Peacock Feather
Clarence H. White photographed a woman holding a peacock feather in 1902. His soft poses and light make it look like a painting.
What does a peacock feather look like?
The Parthenon
Frédéric Boissonnas photographed the Parthenon in Athens in 1902. The temple was built for the goddess Athena in the 400s BC.
How have the columns survived for so long?
Bears One, Dakota Sioux
Gertrude Käsebier made this dignified portrait of Bears One, a Dakota Sioux man, in 1902. She photographed performers from Buffalo Bill's show in her New York studio.
What do you see in his expression?
Steady
William Henry Jackson photographed a hunting dog standing still in profile, around 1902. A pointer holds this pose when it finds game.
How does a dog know to freeze like that?
